m: trai cl. 1. Ā. trāyate (Impv. ˚yatām, 2. sg. ˚yasva and trāsva, pl. ˚yadhvam and trādhvam, RV.; ep. trāti, trātu, trāhi; aor. Subj. trāsate, 2. du. trāsāthe, Prec. trāsīthām, RV.; inf. trātum, MBh. &c.; ind.p. trātvā, BhP. ii, 7, 9) to protect, preserve, cherish, defend, rescue from (gen. or abl.); cf. pari-, saṃ-.
a: trai 1 A. (trāyate, trāta or trāṇa) To protect, preserve, rescue or save from, defend from (usually with abl.); kṣatātkila trāyata ityudagraḥ kṣatrasya śabdo bhuvaneṣu rūḍhaḥ R. 2. 53; Bg. 2. 40; Ms. 9. 138; Bk. 5. 54; 15. 120. -WITH pari to save &c.; paritrāyasva, paritrāyasva (in dramas).

m: traigu˚ṇya n. the state of consisting of 3 threads, tripleness, Mn. ii, 42; Kull.; 3 qualities (śaitya, saugandhya, māndya), Śivarātrivr.
the 3 Guṇas, MBh.; Sāṃkhyak. 14; 18; Tattvas.; Mālav. i, 4; MārkP. l, 3
traigu˚ṇya mfn. having the 3 Guṇas, BhP. xi, 25, 30
a: traiguṇyaṃ 1 The state of consisting of three threads, qualities &c. 2 Triplicity. 3 The three Guṇas or properties (sattva, rajas and tamas) taken collectively; traiguṇyodbhavamatra lokacaritaṃ nānārasaṃ dṛśyate M. 1. 4.

m: traividya mfn. (Pāṇ. iv, 2, 60; Pat.) familiar with tri-vidyā, Lāṭy. viii, 6, 29; Mn.; Yājñ.; MBh.
traividya n. = tri-vidyā, Āp.; Gaut.; Gṛhyās.; Mn. &c.
an assembly of Brāhmans familiar with tri-vidyā, Yājñ.; Hariv. 9578; MārkP. xxiii, 35.
a: traividyaṃ 1 The three Vedas. 2 The study of the three Vedas. 3 An assembly of Brāhmaṇas familiar with the three Vedas. 4 The three sciences. — dyaḥ A Brāhmaṇa versed in the three Vedas; Bg. 9. 20.

m: traya mf(ī)n. (fr. tri, Pāṇ. v, 2, 43) triple, threefold, consisting of 3, of 3 kinds, RV. x, 45, 2; AV. iv, 11, 2; VS. &c. (˚yī vidyā), ‘the triple sacred science’, reciting hymns, performing sacrifices, and chanting [RV., YV., and SV.], ŚBr.; AitBr. &c.
traya n. a triad (chiefly ifc.), ChUp.; KaṭhUp.; Mn. &c.
a: traya a. (yī f.) Triple, threefold, treble, divided into three parts, of three kinds; trayī vai vidyā ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni Śat. Br.; Ms. 1. 23. — yaṃ A triad, a group or collection of three; adeyamāsītvayameva bhūpateḥ śaśiprabhaṃ chatramubhe ca cāmare R. 3. 16; lokatrayaṃ Bg. 11. 20, 43; Ms. 2. 76.

m: trayī—dharma m. the duty enjoined by the 3 Vedas, MBh. iii; Bhag. ix; MārkP. xxi.
tretā f. (fr. traya) and triad, triplet, MBh. xiv, 2759
the 3 sacred fires (= agni-), v, 1559; Hariv. 1410
trey (throw at dice or the side of a die marked with 3 spots), VS. xxx, 18; TS. iv; Mṛcch. ii, 9
‘age of triads’, the 2nd Yuga (or silver age), AitBr.; MuṇḍUp.; ŚāṅkhŚr.; Mn. &c.
a: tretā 1 A triad, triplet. 2 The three sacred fires taken collectively; Ms. 2. 231; R. 13. 37. 3 A particular throw at dice, a cast of three or trey; tretāhṛtasarvasvaḥ Mk. 2. 8. 4 The second of the four Yugas of the Hindus; see yuga.

m: tri m. trayas f. nom. acc. tisras n. trīṇi [trī, RV.; ŚBr. xi] 3 RV. &c. (tribhis & tisṛbhis, &c., RV.; only once tribhis [viii, 59, 5] with the later accentuation, cf. Pāṇ. vi, 1, 177 and 180 f.; gen. trīṇām [RV. x, 185, 1; cf. Pāṇ. vii, 1, 53, Kāś.] and tisṝṇām [RV. viii, 19, 37 and 101, 6], later on [fr. ˚ya] trayāṇām [AitBr.; Mn.] and tisṛṇām [RV. v, 69, 2 against metre; cf. Pāṇ. vi, 4, 4 f.]; ifc., vii, 2, 99 f., Kāś.) ;
tri [cf. τρεῖς, Lat. tres; Goth. threis; &c.]
a: tri num. a. [Uṇ. 5. 66] (declined in pl. only, nom. trayaḥ m., tisraḥ f. trīṇi n.) Three; ta eva hi trayo lokāsta eva traya āśramāḥ &c. Ms. 2. 229; priyatamābhirasau tisṛbhirbabhau R. 9. 18; trīrṇi varṣāṇyudīkṣeta kumāryutṛmatī satī Ms. 9. 90. [Cf. L. tres; Gr. treis; A. S., Zend thri; Eng. three.] Comp. — aṃśaḥ 1 a three-fold share. 2 a third part. 3 three-fourths. — akṣa a. triocular. — akṣaḥ, -akṣakaḥ an epithet of Śiva. — akṣaraḥ 1 the mystic syllable om consisting of three letters; see under a. 2 a match-maker or ghaṭaka (that word consisting of three syllables.) 3 a genealogist. — (rī) knowledge, learning; see vidyā. — aṃkaṭaṃ, -aṃgaṭaṃ 1 three strings suspended to either end of a pole for carrying burdens. 2 a sort of collyrium. — (ṭaḥ) N. of Śiva. — aṃjanaṃ the three kinds of collyrium; i. e. kālāṃjana, rasāṃjana, and puṣpāṃjana. — aṃjalaṃ, -li three handfuls taken collectively. — adhipatiḥ an epithet of Viṣṇu. — adhiṣṭhānaḥ the soul. — (naṃ) spirit, life (catanya). — adhvagā, — mārgagā, -vartmagā epithets of the river. Ganges (flowing through the three worlds). — anīka a. having the three properties of heat, rain and cold; Rv. 3. 56. 3. — (kā) an army consisting of …

m: tri—dhā (tri-), ind. (VPrāt. ii, 44) in 3 ways, in 3 parts, in 3 places, triply, RV. i f., iv; ChUp.; MBh. &c.
a: tridhā ind. In three ways, or in three parts; Ku. 7. 44; Bg. 18. 19.

m: tri—diva n. (m., L.) the 3rd or most sacred heaven, heaven (in general), RV. ix, 113, 9 & AV. (with gen. divas), GopBr.; PraśnUp.; Mn. &c.
tri—jagat n. sg. = jagat traya, BhP. viii; Caurap.; Kathās.; Vet.
tri—mātra mf(ā)n. = ˚trā-kāla, RPrāt.; APrāt.; ŚāṅkhŚr.; 3 in number, MBh. vii
tri—vidha (tri-), mfn. of 3 kinds, triple, threefold, ŚBr. xii; ŚāṅkhŚr.; Mn. &c.
tri—śaṅku m. N. of a sage, TUp. i, 10

of a king of Ayodhyā (aspiring to ascend to heaven in his mortal body, he first requested Vasiṣṭha to perform a great sacrifice for him; on Vasiṣṭha's refusing he applied to Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons, who cursed and degraded him to the rank of a Caṇḍāla [hence called a Caṇḍāla king, Divyāv. xxxiii]; Viśvā-mitra then undertook the sacrifice for him and invited all the gods, who declined to come and thereby so enraged the sage that, by his own power, he transported T˚ to heaven; on his being hurled down again head foremost by the gods, he was arrested in his course by Viśvā-mitra and remained suspended in the sky, forming the southern cross constellation, R. i, 57 ff. (R. G. i, 59) [son of Pṛthu]; Hariv. 730 ff. & VP. iv, 3, 13 f. [son of Trayyāruṇa]; [son of Tri-bandhana] BhP. ix, 7), MBh. i, xiii &c.
N. of a mythical mountain, Divyāv. viii, 293 ff.
tri—śaṅku f. N. of a mythical river, 223 and 295
tri—śaṅku m. pl. N. of thorns, 293
tri—ṇāciketa mfn. one who has thrice kindled the Nāciketa fire or studied the Nāciketa section of Kāṭh.; Āp.; KaṭhUp.; Mn.; Yājñ.; MBh. (Nārāyaṇa xii), VP. iii, 15, 1; MārkP.
tri—ṇāciketa m. pl. N. of 3 Anuvākas of Kāṭh.; Mn. iii, 185; Kull.
